svg.title: Edge-GSE objective results and context trade-offs
svg.desc: Panel A compares DNSMOS with 100 minus bilingual Macro ASR error for offline and streaming systems. Panel B shows four connected Edge-GSE context-sweep observations for DNSMOS and Macro ASR error. The 186.7 millisecond primary result is a separate record and is marked by stars. DelayGSE is an inherited record.
svg.text: URGENT 2025 · 400 bilingual utterances (300 English / 100 Chinese) · aggregate point estimates

g.text: DNSMOS vs macro recognition score · upper right is better

g.aria-label: UniSE: DNSMOS 3.85; Macro ASR error 33.25 percent; Macro recognition score 66.75 percent
DelayGSE, inherited record: DNSMOS 3.77; Macro ASR error 16.95 percent; Macro recognition score 83.05 percent
Bridge: DNSMOS 3.37; Macro ASR error 33.20 percent; Macro recognition score 66.80 percent
Stream.FM: DNSMOS 3.24; Macro ASR error 43.60 percent; Macro recognition score 56.40 percent
FastEnhancer-L: DNSMOS 3.23; Macro ASR error 33.90 percent; Macro recognition score 66.10 percent
DeepFilterNet3: DNSMOS 3.32; Macro ASR error 28.40 percent; Macro recognition score 71.60 percent
Edge-GSE primary, separate record: input context 186.7 milliseconds; DNSMOS 3.62; Macro ASR error 25.45 percent; Macro recognition score 74.55 percent

g.text: Four connected observations · star = independent primary record

svg.text: Macro recognition score = 100 − Macro ASR error; it is direction-aligned, not token accuracy.
Noisy input omitted. † DelayGSE is inherited; external training data and latency definitions are not harmonized.
